tips.comment: Consistent and in-form, Kevin’s Pride boasts strong recent placings (1222), optimal ground suitability, and a capable jockey in JJ Slevin. A standout on speed and stamina metrics, he edges rivals with race-proven class and solid trainer form. Clear top-rated with momentum and favourable odds.

Mary Stanford has not done much but did win on point debut back in March last year. Her second run on rules debut in October was a decent C4 second, only just losing it on the run-in. I would expect more now, second up.
Lucinda Russell trained in the Borders. Three places and a second last time after two successive wins. With that profile and form, should go close.

Saddling 12st last time in a higher class of race, and drops back in class and down to the bottom of the handicap here, which must be a rarity. He hasn’t had the best of 2023, but was better last time after two poor runs prior. The winner of his last race has placed since to frank the form of sorts. He’ll certainly do better over slightly further here, being 6/8 a place at this trip, and any return to his best form off this reduced mark can see him involved in the shake-up. Skelton is 10/19 a place when sending them to Perth in the last 5 years (10 winners from 33 here overall).

Dare To Shout has been a model of consistency this season and looks well placed back in calmer waters today. Last time out he stepped up to Class 2 level at Kelso over a longer trip and ran with credit despite the tougher opposition. Before that, he finished a close second behind Ned Tanner at Carlisle over 2m4f, the same trip he tackles here, beaten just 2¼ lengths by a horse dropping in grade to win well. Dropping back into Class 3 company, where he’s already finished second five times, he looks ready to go one better today. Good luck!

The ground is currently good to soft, good in places & therein lies the chances of Alistair Ralph's 7yo. He's a 7lb better horse on good going & if you add a preference for tight right-handed tracks into the mix, he has to be a bet.

Lucinda Russell has her charge out here with the knowledge that this lad can be happy going this way around. The last time he went chasing was at Uttoxeter, where he jumped right. Today, he can gain lengths with this being his way from one side to the other with jumping. With conditions looking ideal, an excellent run could be on the cards, and Alan Doyle takes three pounds off. If running well here, he may not hold his entry on Friday.

Mister Meggitt easily won his first two starts in bumpers before disappointing when favorite for a Grade 2 at last year's Grand National meeting. He has bounced back this season with a novice hurdle win and last time was beaten just 2.5 lengths in the Grade 1 Sefton Novices' Hurdle. He drops back to listed company here and must have a great chance of winning again.

Horaces Pearl has only had six runs so far but has won the first five of those, including a G2, with the only blip being at Aintree in a G1 last time out. He could bounce back in today's listed company.
Go West, a bumper winner in 2023, then after a long break came back in terrific form, winning plenty of races and looking like a really nice horse. Certainly has a chance here at big odds.

Three wins in a seven-race career so far, and took a decent second at Fairyhouse on return from a 52-day break. The Mullins-owned Irish Raider has a great chance to build on that, and it's Blackmore's only ride for the day.

Has won 4 from the last 6 runs at distances from 21-24f, including two class 2 races at Cheltenham & Musselburgh, both over 24f. Last run was pulled up in the Albert Bartlett, but today sees a big drop in grade and has a 40-day break for a trainer who won this in 2019 with Go Another One and in 2022 with Mahler Mission.

A dual bumper champion who finally triumphed on his 3rd attempt over hurdles in a novice at Stratford last May. He demonstrated significant improvement with a patient ride, while finishing 2nd in the Grade 1 Sefton just 3 weeks ago. While he needs to replicate that performance, a prudent each-way bet at 18/1 is recommended.

YOU OUGHTA KNOW may not be the Willie Mullins trained third-string the market suggests. A later-starting low-mileage seven year old who is twice a Bumper winner which bodes well for his chance of staying this new trip and maybe the market come race-time can reveal more.

It could be worth taking a chance that Royal Infantry will be suited by the step up to 3 miles, especially at his current price. He is by Soldier of Fortune, out of a Presenting mare so there is plenty of stamina in the pedigree and his last run was promising in a Grade 1 behind Salvator Mundi. This is his second race after a wind operation which is often the best time to see improvement.

Lightly raced 6-year-old who has 2 wins and a second-place finish from 3 career starts, including a win over 2m4f in a novice hurdle on penultimate start back in January. Finished second on last start over 2m4f at Ayr, but that form was boosted by the winner who finished third in a Grade 1 at the Aintree Festival. Could run well here if suited by this step up in distance.
Fun Fun Fun should be a slam dunk for the Mullins/Townend team after a G3 win by 13L last month when stepping up to 3 miles for the first time.

I like this mare, but she fell at Kelso with Patrick Wadge. The winner, Grey Dawning, may have put pressure on her. All was going a stride quicker than she likes when coming to grief. She is not meeting anything of that one's potential here. She can act well here, as she showed when winning a hurdle race back in 2023.
Trained by Willie Mullins with Paul Nichols, stable jockey on board. A win last time has been improving and too big a price to ignore each way.
Unlucky at Cheltenham last night when unseating the rider and could have won. Upped in class here and has been well backed, so has a chance.
Won here last June from 3 lbs lower and LTO was narrowly denied in a small field class 2 at Wetherby from this mark. Kept back since, as likely aimed at this meeting due to enjoying the track.

Has his 2nd run since having wind surgery. Dropped 3 lbs for the last run. Dropping back a couple of grades for this race. He's in the right grade this time, having plied his trade in much deeper races. The drop back to class 3 handicaps should see him back competitive. He boasts 3 wins and 1 place from 4 runs in this grade. He's 3/3 in this grade over fences. He's just 1 lb above his last winning mark. He won by 9L on that occasion, hammering Gunsight Ridge with any amount in hand. He goes back right-handed this time. His career-best efforts have come on right-handed tracks. This looks a good opportunity to return to form.

Runs off only 11-0 today & has experienced jockey Sean Bowen in the saddle. The youngest horse in this race, last time out finished super strongly with bags of pace over 2m1f at Plumpton. This trip is his ideal distance & his jumping last time we saw him was fluent & fast. Main danger Etalon looked laboured last time out following wind surgery & carrying 12lb extra this could make all the difference.
Dual winner at Kelso during the autumn who has remained in decent form both over fences and hurdles since. Top weight to deal with today but should still run very well nevertheless.
Placed in 2 of 3 starts last year but has not been seen since July. Returns on a competitive mark and holds an each-way chance.

HAY MEADOW is sired by Wings Of Eagles, a Derby winner. She has shown her tenacity by winning here in a National Hunt flat race and then at Ayr when last seen beating a 1/10 shot, That'll Do Moss. She is five years of age and could be progressing nicely. She is trained by Miss Lucinda Russell, and Connor McCann claims a vital seven pounds.
Olly Murphy, who does well at this meeting and also won this race last year, sends Little Miss Dante with top pilot Sean Bowen up. Looks like their best chance.

Parisian Fashion won comfortably last time when eased towards the finish, so has a bit more in the tank and could be bang in there again even though up 6 lbs. With a decent opening mark on this handicap debut

Won very easily by a wide sixteen lengths last time out at Sedgefield after returning from a wind operation, which seems to have given a huge boost. Up twelve pounds, but it shouldn't be an issue here considering.
Sunday Soldier won five races in a row last season and is still holding form this season. Though disappointing last time, it could bounce back with a first-time tongue tie.

BLEU LAGUNE steps straight out for another try following an eye catching fourth yesterday at Kelso. Those trained by Stuart Crawford have been running well recently and it is interesting that this mare is up in class receiving weight at the foot of the handicap. Likely ahead of her lowly mark she could perform above market expectation.

Henrysbrotherjack has won two of his last three starts. He won at Uttoxeter in December off a mark of 80, and although disappointing off 10 lbs higher at Market Rasen in February, he won off the same mark when successful at Bangor three weeks later. He seemed to benefit from the step up to 2m7f there, and though 10 lbs higher, he can go in again.

Neill Mulholland's only runner here has Mr. S Connor taking three pounds off in the saddle. Was second at Fontwell off this mark and was a beaten favourite but won at that venue previously. To make the long journey to here, they must be thinking they have a solid chance of lifting the £3,973.60 first prize. Interesting.

The 8yo hasn’t been at his best in this campaign but he has raced mostly over fences and was a runner-up two starts back. He was 2nd of 11 at this track this time last year, over hurdles, in a much stronger handicap than this race. He has a 10lb lower mark now. A good jockey booking for this amateur riders’ contest and she can still claim a useful 3lb.

Proven course winner who put in a respectable effort when finishing fourth out of nine runners in a competitive handicap hurdle at Musselburgh (19.8f, good ground) 33 days ago. Now steps back up in trip, which could play to his strengths based on previous performances over longer distances. Last win was off the same mark here and with a 7lb claim, this selection holds good value for an e/w bet.
Suited by trip when scored by 7L off 87 at Ayr three starts back. Finished third off 95 last time out. This stiffer track should suit and looks interesting at an EW price, and cheekpieces reapplied.

From James Moffatt's stable and has Miss Natasha Cookson in the saddle, who has won one race. This is Jet Pack's first run in a handicap and could be proving his worth in the lineup. May be worth a second look, been some support in the market into 9/1 from 14/1.
A son of Nathaniel and might be capable of being involved even though he has not shown much in two maiden races recently. Three miles might bring the best out of him.

This 5yo runs off his lowest mark since his 3yo days, and a very good apprentice is booked who can claim 3lb in this apprentice race. The horse races off 60, and his last 6 win and placed efforts were all off marks between 63 and 65. The horse won a maiden over C&D here and was a head 2nd off a mark of 66 in a handicap, so there's little doubt that he's capable of winning off this mark at a C&D that clearly suits.
Just one win from 19 runs and will welcome a dropped mark and also drop down in class, but improvements are required to have any chance for tomorrow. Also has course experience.
Birkenhead tends to go well here. Last August, he was a winner off a 67 in C5 and comes into today's C6 with a 64. He could go well but is on a bit of a wide draw, so only an EW 4P.

Often races over 7 furlongs and hasn't raced over this trip for a number of years. But has a decent record at this course, placing here a number of times in 2024 at this mark and higher. Last outing was probably needed for fitness. Prior 2 races had been leading with a furlong to run, so shorter trip may suit. A risk but worth an each-way shot.

Military Girl pulled too hard at Musselburgh but showed ability earlier and now returns fresh from a break. Drawn in stall 1 and likely sharper with experience, there’s a fair chance she steps forward here.

The booking of Rossa Ryan looks significant here. He's won on his only other ride on the horse, which was off just a 1 lb lower mark. The horse has been doing most of his racing over 6 furlongs, but I actually think a drop back to 5 furlongs could be ideal, judged on his maiden win over a fast ground 5 furlongs. The 2nd and 3rd are now 100+ and 90+ rated horses, respectively, which all suggests the 11/1 is way too big for this one running off a mark of just 73.
Had a day to forget LTO when 12 of 12 at Southwell last December, but was in good form before that race and should welcome the dropped mark for tomorrow.
Has been competitive since winning here over C&D last July but still has a challenging mark and will need to make some improvements for new yard to have any chance tomorrow.
Magna Grecia Star was really impressive last time, quickening clear like a smart one after a promising debut. Hard to oppose with that kind of form and looks the one they all have to beat.
Animate just didn't look fit enough in the last race, but when boxed, it did switch and run on nicely. This distance should suit.
Ran okay in 3rd latest when trying this 7 furlong trip for the first time, and it is worth noting that its better efforts have come on today's going of good to firm.
Has a very good record fresh-up and caught in that condition here. Course and distance winner and Jason Hart has the experience to put right in the finish if caught in a forward condition.
7 times winner but can be inconsistent. Likes to front run and is drawn well. If getting to the front, will have every chance of claiming at least a place.

Just 1 win for the 4yo filly last year, but plenty near misses and she has ability. Her win did come off her current mark, over this 7f trip and on fast ground. Below par three weeks ago in a 15 runner handicap, but she was coming off a break, a debut for a new yard and most of her rivals were rated 79-87. She should be better for the run, her highest rated rival now is 74 and she has a good apprentice in the saddle claiming a useful 5lb.

Backed by solid form (313-1), Stellarmasterpiece is progressive and rates highly on both class and pace. He has a tactical edge in this race and stays the trip well. Micky Hammond’s yard continues in good form, and this 5-year-old is peaking at the right time.

Lawman's Bliss has done his best work over slightly further, but he’s consistent and this doesn’t look the deepest of races. He should be staying on late and could easily get involved if they go quick early.

Downfield in most of the outings so far. But has a big season ahead off a very handy mark of 54. Double entered and connections could be looking for a quickfire double. Jones has one in the race which looks to shape a similar profile and likely be getting an optimal trip for once and is a strong danger with early support. But gives this mare 9 lbs and returning to turf with a visor could prove very hard to beat. Stays well and could be doing best work late if not caught too tapped for toe.
Not seen since December but had been running well in defeat. Holds an each way chance if returning in the same form

Mojomaker is down to a low historical mark and will definitely like the G/F ground at Catterick today. He has never run at this course but has run well at other tight venues. Has had a break and a warm-up run, so should be spot on today.
Just one win from 21 runs makes poor reading, but crucially that win was over C&D. Now with a dropped mark and a 3lb claimer, I'm hoping he can do the business for the new yard tomorrow.
Six of seven wins have come on the all-weather but made a disappointing reappearance over this course and distance two weeks ago. Holds an each-way chance if building on that performance.

Still just six years old, but Twelfth Knight's handicap mark has dropped from a peak of 87 to a mark of 66. Won on second start after joining Paul Midgley in August 2023 and mostly ran modestly since. In touch with leaders on first run back from wind surgery last time, weakening late on over six furlongs at Newcastle. Could build on that now returned to turf. Market interest. PJ McDonald booked for the ride.

The model I run suggests Brenda's Asking can win this one ahead of More Coko in second and Don't Mind If I Do in third. Brenda's Asking has the highest RPR of the field by a significant margin and helpfully the lowest OR of the field. This leaves what could be considered the best horse of the 7 runners with the lowest weight to carry. Nathan Andrews also claims a massive 10 lbs.

Neil Mulholland's 8yo Milan gelding was left with a bit too much to do when beaten 3 lengths off a rating of 105 at Ascot on his last run, but I think you can mark that run up. He's typically held up and if he's fit after a short break he should be bang there with a 7 pound claimer aboard in what is a winnable heat.
Mikimoto has been well supported here. It has been running some good races without actually winning and surely will break its duck soon at big odds.

Ultra Beat brings strong form (2F35U1) and trainer Daly excels with similar types. He travels well and handles good ground. Off a fair mark and with an ideal pace setup, he rates higher than his rivals here, with an edge in form and recent race fitness.
Progressing nicely, making a fair step forward on his second start over fences. The better ground looked to help him and it is even better here and there should be more to come.

The model I run suggests Almazhar Garde can win this one. Paul O'Brien picks up the reins, who's in good form. This horse is a previous course and distance winner. His form of recent leaves a lot to be desired, but if you wanted to, each way play is viable here at 9s, and there is an extra place on offer on B365.

I am of the opinion that it was traveling the extra half mile that stopped this horse from completing a hat trick. Today, back to the distance of its two wins, should see a better effort. The horse is not ground dependent and is only three pounds higher than its last winning mark.

Versace Twentyone made a winning start under rules when landing a bumper at Roscommon last summer for Gordon Elliott, showing a good turn of foot and plenty of potential. Since joining her current yard, she's produced some encouraging efforts over hurdles, including a solid second in a 19.7f mares' maiden hurdle at Hereford last month on good ground??'her second runner-up finish over timber. That consistency suggests she's heading in the right direction. Now reverting to handicap company, she looks to be on a fair mark and should appreciate the conditions. With her proven ability to travel well and stay on, she's certainly one to consider for each-way support.
Amberelli, making its handicap debut, will be suited to this longer trip. It has been running well and will like the conditions, so it has a chance at big odds.

Disappointing in conditionals the last twice, MISS PEARL is considered back to the same mark as runs at Bangor and Hereford in February. Both of those were near misses, and if she runs back to that standard, then she could get involved from way down the odds market. Still a maiden, which is the concern, but there's still each-way claims.

The model I run suggests Jefferys Cross can win this one. There are plenty of options here at the top of the market, and the difference in win probability from the model is small. However, the weight differential for Jefferys Cross just gives it the nod ahead of some of the other runners in the 6-horse field.

Not At That Price pulled like a train in his first run at Warwick a few weeks ago, and it was a fantastic effort to only be beaten by 6 lengths at the finish. If he settles better here, he looks to have a great chance.

The model I run has picked Egyptian Ginge to win ahead of Not At That Price and Jorah d'Alma in second and third respectively. This horse steps out with the highest RPR of the field, and the lowest weight to carry for this reasonably long 3m trip. Sean O'connor on board is also claiming 5 lbs.
Showed some promise on debut despite finishing a distant 6th of 12 at Doncaster last month. Improvement is likely, and that gives an each-way chance.
Not the most reliable type, Beauld As Brass looks worthy of a flutter, seeing as the odds have halved since the betting opened.

The selection seems to have no opposition with no recent winners in this list except the pick. Dubai Immo won 20 days ago in this distance with a subsequent winner as runner-up. So it deserves plenty of confidence having been raised only 4 lb.
Minimal stakes due to this being an amateur race, but Visibility entered my notebook 9 days ago when denied a clear run over a mile at Pontefract when looking full of running.
Makes Polytrack debut and, if taking to the surface, will go close. Needed the run on reappearance for new stable last time and drops 3lb for this race.

Was going in the right direction but was not able to make the most of a small field when 4 of 5 at Sandown last June. Hoping he has trained well as he's been off for 10 months, and with a dropped mark, might just have a chance.

This horse could have won either of the races it has run in. It has been beaten less than a length both times. It has the favorite Annsar to beat, that horse having finished strongly over this six here. Hopefully, Wise Stars is not so green and will give a more professional account of itself.
Will be a lot fitter today following 2 runs in the last 7 weeks. The drop back to a mile and a half after racing over 2 miles at Kempton last month is appealing.

Very reliable, this one, over whatever distance it tries. Back up to 12 furlongs this afternoon will not be a problem. It has run well over this trip previously, and with 3 places on offer in a 7-runner field, it looks like a no-brainer bet.

Last win 5th Feb over 1m 3f off 69, now runs off 68. Blinkers are on again, last run with them on was a decent 4th as a 16/1 shot where he ran well on turf but struggled to produce extra in final furlong. Used too much up midway through the race and with a more experienced jockey on board here, Kinetic has a great chance.

Innisfree Pearl did well to get her head in front at Brighton and the trainer’s going well, but she’s unproven on the AW and might just need this after the break. Still, she’s going the right way and worth a second look.
Yet to win from 4 starts but did finish a good 2nd on seasonal reappearance last month. Likely to build on that performance and holds every chance

With Ed Walker in decent form and with Saffie Osborne coming for just the one ride here, I'll try a small each way in what doesn't look like a strong maiden. The betting should guide to these, so monitor.

Twice-raced gelding who has done well in both starts, although the drop in trip last time out did him no favors. So, I think he can benefit from going up in trip in what will be his course debut tomorrow.
Recorded a good speed figure over CD LTO, taking a win. Up 2lb from that mark but still looks competitive at bottom weight against its rivals today. Luke Morris takes the mount.

Daisy Roots switched stables and was hammered in the betting. Although it looks a tad high in the ratings, it tried to go for it, only just reeled in. The third that day won yesterday, so there's some substance. Drops a bit in grade, so should go close.
3rd and 1st over CD in the last 6 months, recording some good figures in the process. Competitive weight on its back, winning at a bigger mark previously over the same CD.

Sweet Sister looked stretched over 11f last time so the drop back in trip should suit. She’s usually consistent, the cheekpieces go on, and she’s been eased a few pounds by the handicapper. Could outrun her price if things fall right.

Finishing 7th out of 9 in a handicap at Brighton 10 months ago, this 7-year-old is making his first appearance in nearly a year. With a drop in weight, and a solid track record at this course and distance, he could perform well if he returns in good shape. In-form jockey Luke Morris is likely to secure a favourable outcome. At 25/1, this presents an excellent opportunity for an each-way bet.

TATMEEN is a handicap debutant who has run with some credit through qualifying at this venue. Starting out life in this sphere from his lowly mark is clearly no barrier to success and in a modest looking race at a time of year which could suit an unexposed potential improver he appeals.
Phoenix Moon did it nicely over C&D last time and still looked to have something in hand. Up in the weights now but has momentum and should be right there again if finding a bit more.
Has run to good figures over CD and looks to be its competitive trip of choice. On a good mark and should be up there.

Bit of a punt, but Knockout Blow has two C&D wins here in the last two races, as well as a strong placing record. Hasn't raced for two years though. Has returned from a break strongly in the past, so could get up into the places at 17/1.

Hard not to see this as a two horse race, the other two runners having shown little ability to mount a race. Handlethekettle has been absent for a slightly worrying length of time and returns from wind surgery. Paul Nicholls (SR 14%) is in pretty good form. Jackpot Des Bordes was pretty useful in bumpers (a close second to Celtic Dino) and has form figures of 12 over course and distance at Nicholls' local track. Put in a fair effort when fourth in a Class 3 at Newbury last time out. Jackpot Des Bordes is a big player and the most proven of these so far.

The model I run suggests Breccia can win this ahead of Jacksbar in second and Luna run in third. Breccia has the highest RPR of the field (joint with Jacksbar) but sets out with the second lowest OR. This means he has less weight to carry over this trip, which is practically 3m.

BOBBY'S FORTUNE has to bounce back having been pulled up latest. This yard are finishing the jumps season with a flourish with bundles of recent winners keeping confidence high for all concerned , so a return to form for this well treated runner seems entirely possible.

The model I run simulates this race and suggests Stage Show can get over the line first. Gavin Sheehan picks up the reins, who is in good form. Stage Show steps out with the highest RPR of the field, but the second lowest OR, meaning the weight being carried is a good 15-20 lbs less than the top of the market. It's worth pointing out other jockeys in this race are claiming here, but even with that taken into consideration, Stage Show still carries significantly less than the others around this 2m 3f trip.

Sevenofus was a good second here in March and could well find this trip ideal again on good ground after the last two starts over further. The rider gets her full 7lb claim this time and can at least make the frame.
With questions about several of its main rivals, I expect this horse to win again today. Likes the fast ground (unlike rivals) and is fit and ready (unlike some rivals). The safe choice here.

Nathaniel mare who was last seen at Warwick 169 days ago where finishing 7th/9 however arrives here fresh and in top nick having had a wind op in the process of her break and is now operating on a reduced mark of 90 and can be whole different proposition on this return run in a suitable looking assignment has shown promise over hurdles in past races and now as 5yo she is likely to be much more street wise in this sphere and have more of an impact over on the business end jockey Tristan Durrell takes off a handy 3lb which can only help her cause here and can give Dan Skelton's inmate a promising ride here at Taunton merits consideration

Yet to get his head in front, but he has run well from higher marks in similar contests. Two and a half miles has not suited him the last twice, so the return to the minimum trip is going to be a plus for him.

KOTGAR is another runner for bang-in-form trainer Evan Williams and this unexposed four year old is well bred suggesting an opening handicap hurdles mark of 100 is within hs compass. He has qualified quietly , but this minimum hurdles trip looks suitable on pedigree and the market can help us.

JUBILEE GOLD steps back up in trip which should be in his favour. This looks competitive enough for a handicap at this time of year under the NH code , but still with not too many miles on his clock as a nine year old he could well be ready to peak tonight.

The model I run suggests El Gavilan can take a step forward here and get over the line first. He's the youngest horse in the running but steps out with the joint highest RPR and carries the joint lowest weight of the field over the 2m 3f trip. Adam Wedge picks up the reins for this step down in class (moving from class 3 prior races where he placed in 3 races on the spin to class 4 here now) and I think is good value at 8.5s.

The model I run suggests Bob Bishop should win this one ahead of Top Tier Gossip in second and Robin Blue in third, respectively. Joint highest RPR of the field and steps out carrying the lowest weight. Placed here at Taunton in late March with the same 2m NHF.
